first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ. Memory_86 demonstrated that shortening onboarding improved completion and adoption; memory_31 showed signup simplification lifted first-week activation. Both directly address current performance gaps. Verifying memory_86 confirms the magnitude and durability of the completion lift. Memory_73 is verified to rule out promotional_pricing: it showed material retention damage in SMB segments, and applying it now risks compounding our revenue quality problems despite competitor pressure. A standard_experiment on simplified onboarding targets the root metrics we're losing without incurring the retention risk that would undermine sustainable long-term revenue. The referral_incentive path (memory_57) is strong but requires existing customer base momentum; we need to restore baseline activation first. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is viable but addresses a different customer segment than our current pain point.

mid.rationale: Verified data confirms memory_86: shortened onboarding delivered +13% completion, -2.1 days time-to-value, and +3% retention lift. This directly addresses both current gaps (completion -4%, activation -6% QoQ). Memory_73 verification reconfirms that promotional pricing trades sustainable revenue for short-term acquisition—exactly wrong for our primary objective in a competitive environment where we cannot afford cohort quality decay. Simplify_onboarding is the highest-confidence play: it has proven durable impact on completion and retention, targets our immediate performance shortfall, and carries no downstream value risk. Memory_91 (activation messaging) is complementary; pairing both onboarding simplification and in-product activation nudges maximizes the recovery lift. This preserves our ability to pivot if competitor pricing proves more destructive than current data suggests, while committing capacity to the intervention with strongest evidence for sustainable revenue.

final2.rationale: Competitive pressure is acute, but memory_73 remains dispositive: promotional pricing won against a price-sensitive cohort at -12% 30-day retention. That cohort did not survive renewal. Deploying matching discounts now would accelerate churn in the accounts we're trying to save and lock us into a margin-destructive spiral with no retention foundation. The downstream value risk is flagged because leadership demand may override rational analysis, but the evidence is clear: price-matching fails on sustainable revenue. Scaling simplify_onboarding to small_guarded_test preserves the option to pivot while deploying the highest-confidence intervention we have. Shortened onboarding +13% completion and +3% retention is our only lever that improves both activation and cohort quality simultaneously. This buys time for week-two decision-making without sacrificing margin or customer lifetime value. If churn accelerates despite onboarding improvement, we reassess with next week's verification budget. For now, competing on product experience velocity and activation depth is more defensible than competing on price from a position of weakening fundamentals.
